messages:
alex: Hi all  first-week networking weirdness on Windows WSL2. I started the compose stack (db + redis) and the app running in WSL can't hit Redis on docker, rspecs show `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379`. I tried host.docker.internal but it doesn't resolve from WSL. Any quick fix?

maya: Welcome Alex! On WSL2 you usually need to be careful whether the app runs in WSL or Windows host. If your app is in WSL and docker is the Windows Docker Desktop backend, `host.docker.internal` may not be visible. Two quick approaches: 1) map ports and talk to `localhost:6379` from WSL if Docker Desktop exposes them, or 2) add host-gateway mapping in compose so `host.docker.internal` resolves.

oleg: We use this snippet in our compose when folks are on Windows:
```yaml
services:
  app:
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
```
That requires Docker >= 20.10 and using compose v2. Then `host.docker.internal` works inside containers.

azra: small note: `network_mode: host` is available on Linux but not on Docker Desktop for Windows/WSL in the same way, so avoid that here.

devex-bot: Dev docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/dev-setup/windows-wsl2 (search for "host-gateway" example). Also check `docker info` for WSL integration settings. :robot_face:

alex: I added extra_hosts and restarted but still `ECONNREFUSED`. `docker ps` shows redis has `0.0.0.0:6379->6379/tcp`. From WSL I can `curl http://127.0.0.1:6379` and it times out.

maya: If `curl` times out, Docker Desktop might not be exposing ports to WSL network. Try `docker run --rm -p 63790:6379 redis:7` and then from WSL `nc -vz 127.0.0.1 63790` to confirm reachability. If that fails, ensure WSL integration is enabled in Docker Desktop settings (Resources -> WSL Integration).

oleg: Also make sure you haven't got Windows firewall blocking Docker or WSL. We had one new hire where corporate AV blocked the bridge network. Temporarily disable firewall/AV to test.

alex: ok `docker run -p 63790:6379 redis:7` from Windows powershell shows mapped port, but from WSL `nc -vz 127.0.0.1 63790` still fails. Docker Desktop WSL integration is ON.

maya: In that case check the WSL distro's /etc/resolv.conf and `cat /etc/hosts` for stray entries. Some setups have a stale `hosts` entry pointing `127.0.0.1` to loopback incorrectly. Also try `ping $(cat /etc/resolv.conf | grep nameserver | awk '{print $2}')` to see DNS reachability.

azra: Another reliable pattern we add to onboarding: expose services on a high port and reference `127.0.0.1` from host apps, or run the app in a container so it just uses `host.docker.internal` or service names. For WSL devs we often run everything in WSL containers to avoid cross-host network issues.

devex-bot: Quick checklist: 1) confirm port mapped with `docker ps` 2) test from Windows host and from WSL separately 3) try ephemeral port map e.g. `-p 127.0.0.1:63790:6379` 4) check firewall/AV 5) try running the app in a container as a workaround.

oleg: If you want, I can hop on a quick call and we can try the `extra_hosts: host-gateway` plus a named network approach. Often it's a tiny Windows host quirk.

alex: Thanks everyone  I disabled corporate AV temporarily and `nc` to 63790 from WSL works now. Extra_hosts + switching to high port mapping fixed it. I'll update my onboarding notes with the firewall/AV tip. Appreciate it!

maya: Great  welcome aboard. If you want, open a PR adding a short Windows troubleshooting section to infra/README.md and tag @devex for review.
